status_rules.in_progress: the ONE feature currently being worked on — only one at a time
status_rules.blocked: cannot proceed due to a documented issue; the issue must be in notes
status_rules.passing: verification executed verbatim AND evidence file recorded

demo_mode_rules.live: must be fully dynamic end to end — part of the golden path
demo_mode_rules.seeded: implement as realistic pre-loaded data, not a live pipeline

features.title: Shared Neon Postgres + pgvector
features.user_visible_behavior: Every teammate's backend connects to one shared database; data ingested by one person is visible to all.
verification: Create the Postgres project and note the connection string.
Run in a SQL console: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
Put DATABASE_URL in .env on two different machines (never commit .env).
Machine A: python backend/scripts/check_db.py --write
Machine B: python backend/scripts/check_db.py --write
Either machine: python backend/scripts/check_db.py --read -> prints PASS and lists rows from BOTH machines.
Save that terminal output to evidence/infra-001/two-machine-check.txt
features.notes: Blocks everything. Free tier is enough. Share the connection string in the team channel, never in git. Verified by backend/scripts/check_db.py, which also proves the pgvector extension is live by running a distance operator. BLOCKED 2026-08-23: connectivity confirmed from one machine (PostgreSQL 18.6, pgvector 0.8.6, distance operator exercised). Cannot pass until a second machine runs --write, which is the whole claim of the feature. Unblocks the moment a teammate runs the three setup lines.

features.title: Green baseline — requirements.txt, package.json, ./init.sh passes
features.user_visible_behavior: A teammate clones the repo, runs ./init.sh, and gets a passing verification plus the start command.
verification: On a clean clone: ./init.sh
Exits 0 and prints 'Verification passed.'
RUN_START_COMMAND=1 ./init.sh boots uvicorn and GET /health returns 200.
features.notes: Until this passes, the 'fix the baseline first' rule in CLAUDE.md is unenforceable. Needs at least one trivial pytest so the suite is non-empty.

features.title: Frozen API contract (docs/api-contract.md)
features.user_visible_behavior: Not user visible. Five frontend people build against this file with mocks while the backend catches up.
verification: Every endpoint in the golden path has a documented method, path, request shape and response shape.
A frontend teammate builds one page against the mock without asking a clarifying question.
features.notes: HOUR-2 DELIVERABLE. Sushree is the bottleneck for five people; this file is how they parallelize. Freeze at hour 4. 2026-08-23: docs/api-contract.md drafted covering all 32 features / 46 endpoints (coverage check in evidence). Stays in_progress -- the second verification step requires a frontend teammate to build a page against the mock without asking a clarifying question, which cannot be self-certified.

features.title: LLM/translation provider interface + disk cache + fallback + mock
features.user_visible_behavior: Not user visible. The demo replays identically and works with no internet.
verification: Call the tutor endpoint twice with the same input; second call is served from cache (log line or timing proves it).
Set the GLM key to garbage; the fallback provider answers.
Set PROVIDER=mock and disconnect wifi; the golden path still completes end to end.
features.notes: Cache key = sha256(model + prompt). This is the single highest-leverage insurance policy for demo day.

features.title: Cloudflare tunnel + VITE_API_BASE wiring for remote team
features.user_visible_behavior: A teammate on another laptop runs the frontend locally and it talks to Sushree's backend.
verification: Start cloudflared; copy the https URL into a teammate's frontend/.env.local as VITE_API_BASE.
Teammate loads the app and successfully logs in against the remote backend.
CORS allows the vite dev origin.
features.notes: Demo must run on at least two laptops. Tunnel URL changes on restart — repost it each time.

features.title: Email + password signup, login, logout
features.user_visible_behavior: User signs up with email and password, logs in, lands on the dashboard for their role, and can log out.
verification: Sign up a new student; password is stored as a pbkdf2_sha256 hash, never plaintext (check the DB row).
Log in with the correct password -> token returned and stored.
Log in with the wrong password -> 401, no token.
Authenticated request to a protected route succeeds; the same route without a token returns 401.
Logout invalidates the token; the next request returns 401.
features.notes: Opaque UUID token in a sessions table. NO JWT. pbkdf2_sha256, NOT bcrypt (native build fails on Windows). Roles: student, teacher, admin.

features.title: Forgot password — UI only
features.user_visible_behavior: Login page has a 'Forgot password?' link opening a screen that accepts an email and shows a confirmation message.
verification: Click 'Forgot password?' on the login page.
Enter an email, submit, and see the confirmation copy.
No network request is made and no backend route exists.
features.notes: EXPLICITLY UI-ONLY per team decision. Do not build email sending or reset tokens.

features.title: PyMuPDF ingestion to page-anchored chunks
features.user_visible_behavior: Not directly visible, but every citation shown to a student resolves to a real book and page.
verification: Ingest a real course PDF.
Query the chunks table: every row has doc_id, page_no and a char span.
Pick 3 chunks at random and confirm the text really appears on that page of the PDF.
features.notes: Page numbers are non-optional — 'Show Source' depends on them. Run only on Sushree's machine; ship backend/data/dump.sql.

features.title: Embeddings + pgvector retrieval with citations
features.user_visible_behavior: An explanation comes back with the specific chunks it was grounded in, each carrying a book title and page number.
verification: Embed the corpus with bge-small-en-v1.5 (384-dim).
Query a topic that IS in the corpus; top-3 chunks are on-topic by manual read.
Response includes citations with resolvable book + page.
features.notes: Brute-force cosine. NO ivfflat/hnsw index — corpus is small and an index is a failure mode.

features.title: Evidence check + syllabus alignment score
features.user_visible_behavior: Every lesson and explanation card shows a syllabus-alignment percentage.
verification: A well-covered topic scores high (>70%).
A tangential topic scores visibly lower.
The same score value appears on the student lesson card and in the API response.
features.notes: RUBRIC FEATURE. top-k cosine + one LLM entailment check -> percentage. Build by hour 8.

features.title: Refuse when evidence is insufficient + uncertainty flag
features.user_visible_behavior: Asked something the curriculum does not cover, the tutor says it lacks evidence instead of guessing — and the teacher sees it in Uncertainty Flags.
verification: Ask an off-syllabus question; the tutor refuses and does not fabricate an answer.
A row appears in uncertainty_flags with the query and the score.
That row is visible on the teacher dashboard without any extra wiring.
features.notes: RUBRIC FEATURE. One feature, two dashboards — the refusal auto-populates teacher-004.

features.title: Graded-work guardrail
features.user_visible_behavior: Asked to solve a graded assignment question, the tutor declines and offers scaffolded hints instead of the answer.
verification: Paste a seeded assignment question verbatim; the tutor refuses to produce the final answer.
It returns hints/scaffolding instead.
A normal conceptual question on the same topic is still answered fully.
features.notes: RUBRIC FEATURE. Guard prompt + rule: if the query matches an assignment chunk in the KB, refuse.

features.title: Course summary on login
features.user_visible_behavior: On first login a student sees what's in scope: which books, which pages, which topics.
verification: Log in as the seeded student.
Course summary lists real books and page ranges drawn from the ingested corpus.

features.title: Prerequisite gap check (diagnostic test)
features.user_visible_behavior: Student takes a short diagnostic and receives a gap list — not a grade.
verification: Take the diagnostic answering some items wrong.
Output is a list of named prerequisite gaps.
No overall score or grade is displayed anywhere on the result screen.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 1. The 'gap list, not a grade' framing is a judging point — do not add a score.

features.title: Gap-to-lesson mapping + alignment score on the card
features.user_visible_behavior: Each identified gap links to approved material, with a syllabus-alignment percentage on the lesson.
verification: Click a gap from the diagnostic result.
A lesson loads sourced from the approved KB with a visible alignment percentage.
The percentage matches the value in the API response.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 2.

features.title: Show Source
features.user_visible_behavior: Every explanation card links to the exact book and page it was grounded in.
verification: Open any lesson card and click Show Source.
It names a real book and page number.
Open the PDF at that page and confirm the content matches.
features.notes: Cheap, highly visible to judges, directly quoted in the problem statement.

features.title: Scoped practice generator
features.user_visible_behavior: Practice problems are generated for the student's identified gaps, not random course-wide problems.
verification: From a specific gap, generate practice.
Every generated item is about that gap's concept.
Generating from a different gap produces visibly different items.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 3.

features.title: Post-quiz misconception check with confirm/deny
features.user_visible_behavior: After a wrong answer, the AI names the likely misconception behind it and asks the student to confirm or deny.
verification: Answer a practice question wrong in a specific, predictable way.
The named misconception plausibly matches that wrong answer, not a generic one.
Click Confirm; a confirmed_diagnosis row is written.
Click Deny on another; it is recorded as denied and does NOT feed the heatmap.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 4 — the single most important feature in the build. Match against seeded error patterns per problem type.

features.title: Per-topic mastery tracker
features.user_visible_behavior: Concept-level view of which ideas are solid and which are shaky — not one score, not time-on-task.
verification: Open the mastery view; concepts are listed individually with a solid/shaky state.
No single aggregate score and no time-tracking is shown.
features.notes: The absence of a single score and of time-on-task is deliberate — it is the anti-surveillance stance.

features.title: Misconception heatmap (live-updating)
features.user_visible_behavior: Per topic, the most common wrong mental models across the class, ranked by confirmed-diagnosis frequency.
verification: Note the current count for a misconception on the teacher dashboard.
On the second laptop, have the student confirm that misconception.
Refresh the teacher dashboard; the count has incremented.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 5 — the closing beat of the demo. Poll on an interval; do NOT build websockets.

features.title: Reasoning-path breakdown
features.user_visible_behavior: For a given problem, the top confirmed error patterns, each with one anonymized example.
verification: Open a problem's breakdown.
Error patterns are ranked and each shows one example.
No student name or identifier appears anywhere.
features.notes: Anonymization is a judging point — verify no names leak in the API response, not just the UI.

features.title: Prerequisite gap map
features.user_visible_behavior: Class-level view of which foundational concepts a chunk of students are missing, tied to the current topic.
verification: Open the gap map for a topic.
Foundational concepts are shown with the share of the class missing each.

features.title: Uncertainty flags panel
features.user_visible_behavior: Cases where the tutor said 'not enough evidence' are surfaced for teacher review rather than failing silently.
verification: Trigger a refusal as a student.
The flag appears in the teacher panel with the query and the alignment score.
features.notes: Comes almost free from rag-003. High judging value for very little work.

features.title: Before/after reteach tracking
features.user_visible_behavior: Shows whether a specific misconception is shrinking after a targeted reteach — not whether overall scores rose.
verification: Open a misconception that has a seeded reteach event.
Before and after frequencies are both shown, with the delta.
features.notes: Seed two time buckets. Do not build a real longitudinal pipeline in 36 hours.

features.title: Auto-suggested reteach unit with teacher approval
features.user_visible_behavior: AI proposes a short lesson or practice set for the class's most common misconception; the teacher approves or edits before assigning.
verification: Open the top misconception and generate a reteach suggestion.
Edit the text, then approve.
It becomes assigned; without approval it is never visible to a student.
features.notes: The approval gate is the human-in-the-loop story. Never auto-assign.

features.title: AI-sourced content verification queue
features.user_visible_behavior: Material the AI found via web search sits in a queue for teacher approval before any student can see it.
verification: Open the queue with seeded pending items.
Approve one; it becomes available.
Confirm a pending item cannot be reached from any student view.
features.notes: Seed the items. Do NOT build live web search in 36 hours — the queue itself is the point.

features.title: Curriculum upload and versioning
features.user_visible_behavior: Admin uploads syllabus/textbooks/notes per course with chapter and page mapping; older versions stay archived.
verification: Upload a PDF as admin; it appears in the course's material list.
Upload a replacement; the previous version is still listed as archived, not deleted.
features.notes: Upload by a verified admin counts as approval for this build — per the feature plan.

features.title: Course and institution structure with prerequisites
features.user_visible_behavior: Departments, courses, and which courses are prerequisites for which others.
verification: View the structure; a course shows its prerequisite courses.
Gap detection for that course references the correct prior course.
features.notes: This is what makes gap detection reference the right prior course — seed it correctly.

features.title: Audit log and version history
features.user_visible_behavior: Records who uploaded or changed what, and when.
verification: Perform an upload as admin.
A log entry appears with actor, action and timestamp.
features.notes: The human-in-the-loop trail. Cheap to build, good to point at during the pitch.

features.title: Multilingual interaction via Sarvam
features.user_visible_behavior: Student picks a language; questions and explanations work in it, with citations preserved.
verification: Switch to Hindi and ask a question in Hindi.
The answer comes back in Hindi.
Citations still resolve to the correct English source book and page.
The alignment score is unchanged from the English equivalent question.
features.notes: Pipeline: translate to English -> retrieve -> answer in English -> translate back. Vector space stays English-only.

features.title: Accessible interaction — read-aloud, font size, contrast
features.user_visible_behavior: Student can have any explanation read aloud, enlarge text, and switch to high contrast.
verification: Click read-aloud on a lesson; browser speechSynthesis speaks it.
Increase font size; layout does not break.
Toggle high contrast; text remains readable throughout.
Tab through the student dashboard using only the keyboard and reach every control.
features.notes: speechSynthesis is free and needs no API. shadcn/Radix gives keyboard nav and ARIA for free. ~40 min for a whole judging criterion.

features.title: Two-laptop golden path rehearsal
features.user_visible_behavior: The full demo runs start to finish on two laptops without a manual fix.
verification: Laptop A runs the student flow; laptop B shows the teacher dashboard.
Run docs/demo-script.md verbatim end to end.
Repeat it a second time from a clean state with no manual DB edits.
Repeat once with wifi disabled and PROVIDER=mock.
features.notes: Rehearse at least twice before the deadline. Budget the last 3 hours for this — do not spend them on features.
